quotes.text: Radar evaluates each incoming dispute against the dispute resolution rules you create. If a dispute matches the criteria for any rule, we automatically resolve it.
For all dispute resolution rules, the action is `Resolve dispute`.
For destination charges with `on_behalf_of` set, `on_behalf_of` takes precedence.
For decimal currencies (for example, **usd**), rules use the base currency unit rather than sub units (for example, dollars, not cents).

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules/disputes, November 7, 2026 documents an eligible merchant creating dispute resolution rules when its plan supports dispute prevention. Radar evaluates each incoming dispute and automatically resolves it by refund if any configured rule matches. The action is Resolve dispute and the conditions use a dedicated attribute set (new raw line 9 and new raw lines 11-24). May 10, 2026 describes the same engine and action while naming Stripe Radar or Radar for Fraud Teams plus dispute-prevention signup (old raw line 8 and old raw lines 10-23). The separate November Dispute prevention preview describes signup via Dispute settings. Both capture attributes distinguish disputed from original payment amount, convert it with base units such as dollars, and prioritize the on_behalf_of account for destination charges when present. Card brand only lists visa and mc; network reason codes are Visa only (new raw lines 26-40, old raw lines 25-39). source-stripe-radar-rules-disputes reflects the core May mechanics, but lacks the newer plan qualification, the Connect precedence and decimal-currency unit semantics, and a warning about the inconsistent threshold explanation.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules/disputes, update source-stripe-radar-rules-disputes and retain both dated factual captures. November 7, 2026 changes eligibility wording to plan support for dispute prevention, compared with May 10, 2026 naming Stripe Radar or Radar for Fraud Teams plus signup (new raw line 9, old raw line 8). The connected November prevention guide still directs merchants to sign up. No exact tier assignment, entitlement change or end to signup follows from this wording. Both sources show an inclusive <= 10.00 rule and say 10 USD or less, then separately call the condition < 10.00. Preserve the conflict at the 10 USD boundary (new raw lines 17-22, old raw lines 16-21). The underlying matching/refund behavior and exact dispute-amount and Connect account boundaries persist (new raw lines 26-40, old raw lines 25-39). Table formatting and emphasis are presentational, while the Query Disputes and Dispute Prevention retargets and added Rules Reference are navigation (new raw lines 42-48, old raw lines 41-46). Keep the reciprocal stripe-radar route with the plan qualification, and retain the separate dispute-prevention and transaction-rules context plus a Rules Reference syntax route. Do not infer dispute eligibility from generic transaction rules.
